clue.text: Well dressed newly-married male journalist

parts.note: a groom is a man on his wedding day
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A society column admires a smartly turned-out bridegroom who writes for a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone neat and well turned out in appearance is said to be smartly presented this way.

clue.text: Looks for George pierce (son)

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for the name George
to lance is to pierce, as a surgeon does a boil
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent looks for George, who has a son called Pierce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pierce' poses as a name in brackets with 'son'; it is the verb to lance.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick peeks or brief glimpses at something.

clue.text: Frequently defined as "decimal"

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry says that some word commonly means decimal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits as OF TEN: decimal means relating to the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently means many times, repeatedly; decimal, read as two words, is based on the number ten.

clue.text: Coins a word for "sweets"

explanation.surface: Someone invents a new term for confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coins' is a verb: the Royal Mint stamps money, so to coin is to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins as a verb means makes money at a mint; sweets are peppermints, small sugary lozenges.

clue.text: Take away a bit of land to support the lower classes

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
a tract is an area or stretch of land

explanation.surface: A plan to remove some land in order to help the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: UK market research grades households A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so DE is the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish or subtract from the worth of something, as a flaw does from its value.

clue.text: Gets hold of the dog in the bishops' offices

indicators.note: the dog's word is placed inside the word for the bishops' offices

parts.note: a bishop's see is his diocese or seat of office; plural SEES
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a stray dog that has wandered into the diocesan offices.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something safe or fasten it into one's possession is to obtain it firmly.

clue.text: Realist has to change and become a little more witty

indicators.note: the letters of realist are made to change their order

explanation.surface: A dour realist must loosen up and become funnier.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty humour is racy or sharp, so the comparative means somewhat sharper or earthier in wit.

clue.text: It may produce tears in a line of children?

explanation.surface: Little ones walking in a queue are reduced to crying.
explanation.walkthrough: Crocodile tears are false weeping; in Britain a crocodile is also a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile is said to weep while eating its prey, and a two-by-two file of pupils on a walk shares its name.

clue.text: Procedure for outfit requiring higher degree and character

parts.note: rig is informal for an outfit of clothes
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree above a bachelor's
a role is a character an actor plays

explanation.surface: Getting a costume demands an advanced qualification and the right personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, complicated process or rigmarole of formalities and fuss.

clue.text: Models who look after the children

explanation.surface: The people posing for the artist also do some babysitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Models pose for portrait painters; babysitters mind youngsters while parents are out.

clue.text: Relative rumoured to have taken south African place before birth

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed around by word of mouth, so we want a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: an auntie is a relative, and the word said aloud gives ANTE
Natal is a province on the east coast of South Africa

explanation.surface: Gossip says a relative has moved into a South African region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumoured' calls for a sound-alike of the relative; the Latin prefix for 'before' is what you hear. Natal was a South African province, now part of KwaZulu-Natal.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes care or classes given to a mother during pregnancy, the period preceding a baby's arrival.

clue.text: Should an expression of disgust be found in holy books?

indicators.note: the exclamation is said to sit inside the abbreviation for the holy books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first group of books of the Bible
ugh is what people exclaim at something revolting

explanation.surface: A pious reader wonders whether the scriptures contain any cry of revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both modal verbs express obligation or duty: you must, morally, do it.

clue.text: Game that's American — as tactics revealed

indicators.note: the letters are exposed inside the run of words American as tactics

explanation.surface: A remark that some pastime is distinctly American, judging by its tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and the word break hide the run: americ(AN AS TAC)tics.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy-style card pastime played with two packs, originating in Uruguay.

clue.text: Ignore a distressing period

indicators.note: to distress is to damage or knock about, so the letters of ignore a are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to look away from something upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressing' looks like the period's description, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric age after the Bronze Age when metal tools of that kind were first made.

clue.text: Butcher (at last) plays with good humour

indicators.note: the bracketed phrase points to the final letter of the next word, plays

parts.note: laughter is the sound of merriment and good humour

explanation.surface: A butcher who finally puts on shows full of jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill brutally or in great numbers, as a butcher does with animals.

clue.text: Hanger-on had a very quiet finish — a good point

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
an end is a finish or conclusion
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone who had a hushed ending to a performance made a fine remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An attachment or limb hanging from something; figuratively a dependent follower.

clue.text: Ensure sentry finishes early, with ease, say, to support worker

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after
the word for a sentry stops before its last letter

parts.note: a guard stands sentry
an ant is the stock worker of crosswords, a worker ant

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the word: ease sounds like E's, two letter Es

parts.note: said aloud, ease sounds like E's, the plural of the letter E

explanation.surface: To be certain, a guard leaves his shift early, easily backing up a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes early' cuts D from GUARD. 'ease, say' is a play on sound: ease sounds like 'E's', two Es, which go under ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to make certain it will happen, as a pledge does.

clue.text: Solid performance from one's heroes

indicators.note: a performance can be a fuss or a palaver, so the letters of solid are thrown about

explanation.surface: A rock-solid show from the people one looks up to.
explanation.definitionFit: People one worships or admires greatly, like film stars or sporting champions.

clue.text: Three coppers and a mug?

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper; P, a penny, is a copper coin, so three coppers are CU, P and P
P stands for a penny, a copper coin
a second penny, another P

explanation.surface: Three policemen and someone easily fooled walk into a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like policemen, but gives the metal's symbol CU and two pennies. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea, and the question mark flags 'mug' as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a cup of tea, which may well be served in a large drinking vessel with a handle.

clue.text: Two firms working with original Spanish wraps

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a second firm, another CO
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: the first letter of Spanish is its original letter

explanation.surface: Two companies collaborate with a Spanish partner on packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to envelop or swathe protectively, as a silkworm's casing surrounds it.

clue.text: Unlike poor friend, left without a starter

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged
the word left loses its opening letter, like a meal missing its first course

explanation.surface: A complaint that a pal has been left without an opening course at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a starter' trims left to EFT, and 'poor' shuffles EFT with FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are dissimilar or not alike are distinct from one another.

clue.text: Mocks Danish leader's travels across England

indicators.note: the letters for Danish leader and travels stretch across the abbreviation for England
the leader of the word Danish is its first letter

parts.note: rides means travels on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A Danish king's journeys across England are ridiculed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule or scoff at someone with contempt.

clue.text: Plenty are taken in by familiar wreckage

indicators.note: the word for plenty sits inside the short form of familiar

parts.note: fam is informal shorthand for family or familiar
lots means plenty, a great many

explanation.surface: A crowd is fooled by debris that looks familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating debris from a shipwreck, paired with jetsam.

clue.text: Raised a glass and got burnt

explanation.surface: A celebrant lifted a drink and then got sunburnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a glass is drinking a health; bread browned under a grill is scorched.

clue.text: Horseman of old

parts.note: read literally, a horse-man: a creature from Greek myth with a human torso on a horse's body, not a rider

explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is a knight or cavalryman; the trick is to take 'Horseman' literally as half horse, half man.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek mythology's half-human, half-equine beast is literally a horse-man of ancient legend.

clue.text: Instrument in an old mini, say, indicator not actually starting

parts.note: the Mini is a small British motor car, so it is an example of a car

indicators.note: the opening letters of indicator, not and actually are taken

explanation.surface: Someone describes the indicator lights on an old Mini car that don't quite come on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' looks like part of the car story, but it takes the first letters of 'indicator not actually'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, sometimes called a sweet potato.

clue.text: Roughly defining a session

parts.note: a bout is a spell or session of activity

explanation.surface: A dictionary meaning: roughly means a single sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximately or more or less, as in about five o'clock.

clue.text: Gather sign of deer reduces the odds

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of sign of deer are removed, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A hunter concludes that a deer's track lowers the betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: From SIGNOFDEER, removing the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on leaves the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce or conclude from evidence, as in 'I gather you are leaving'.

clue.text: Love to leave these paintings?

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, written O
to part is to go away or depart

explanation.surface: An art lover would like to say goodbye to certain pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1960s movement of abstract works using optical illusions, so its products are canvases of that style.

clue.text: Dance hall many agree causes upset

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub or hall for dancing
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for a large number
to fit is to suit or agree with, as when two accounts fit

explanation.surface: Lots of people concur that the local dance venue causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass or disconcert someone, making them uneasy, is to throw them off balance.

clue.text: Radios could be reset so

indicators.note: the letters of reset so could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A technician notes that the radios might be tuned again that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound systems or record players with two channels; older hi-fi units often included a tuner.

clue.text: Dreamt about university of the third age?

indicators.note: about means in disorder, so the letters of dreamt and U are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone fantasised about a university for retired people.
explanation.walkthrough: The University of the Third Age is a British learning network for retired people; here 'third age' just means older years.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown older, mature in years, as people in later life are.
